newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Creditors choose 18 Kia Group units for bail-out.
newsitem.headline: Creditors choose 18 Kia Group units for bail-out.

text.p: Creditors to South Korea's Kia Group selected 18 of its 38 affiliates for rescue, a statement from the Korea First Bank said on Tuesday.
Included in the bail-out plan are the flagship carmaker Kia Motors, Asia Motors, Kia Steel, Kisan, Kia Precision, Kia Service and 12 other unlisted units.
The Korea First Bank, Kia's major creditor, announced the plan in the press room of the central Bank of Korea.
Figures released from the Korea Federation of Banks showed net credit to Kia Group by South Korean financial institutions totalled 9.54 trillion won at the end of May, 1997.
A Korea First statement said worsening business performances of some major units had burdened Kia Motors.
The statement said some financial institutions had called in loans and tended to avoid extending fresh money to the Kia Group, limiting the conglomerate's ability to generate more funds.
"We decided to bail out Kia Group to help normalise its business as it involves the nation's strategic business," the statement said.
Kia Group sought a bail-out and creditors selected 18 affiliates for rescue, a Bank of Korea official said.
